tasks.short: Plan store budgets and approve payments and merchandise returns within delegated limits.

steps.what: Gather sales, spending, stock commitments and current budget figures.
Prepare budget scenarios using sales expectations, costs and planned purchases.
Discuss assumptions and choose spending priorities with the store manager.
Approve the budget within delegated authority or escalate it.
Check payment requests against invoices, receipt records, budget and approval limits.
Authorize spending or resolve and escalate payment exceptions.
Release authorized payments through the bank's approval process.
Check referred return requests against receipt details and return policy.
Inspect returned goods when condition or damage affects the decision.
Decide the return exception and explain the outcome to the customer.
Record the return decision, authorization and stock disposition.
Process the authorized refund or exchange and issue a receipt.
Review budget variances and identify spending requiring intervention.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} records and generates budget scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}, with variances shown in the {BI}. Configure checks and approval routing in the {ERP} and {PROCUREMENT}, retaining budget, spending and bank-release approvals in the {ERP} and {BANK}. Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} to check return eligibility, capture the supervisor's exception decision and process only authorized refunds, with duplicate and amount controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget scenarios need reconciled sales, commitments and spending. Payment and return controls often sit in separate systems, while exceptions depend on delegated authority and customer context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing systems often support approval rules, exports and transaction interfaces. AI-assisted coding can shorten development of missing mappings, scenario calculations and reconciliation checks; no model breakthrough is required.
tasks.still_hard: Stock commitments, tax treatment and refund status must reconcile correctly. Physical condition, disputed customer accounts and commercial tradeoffs still need people. Interfaces and payment controls can dominate delivery cost.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor balances customer trust, stock condition, trading priorities and spending constraints, and takes responsibility for exceptions.

ambition.what: Daily corrective spending decisions using projected store budget overruns.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling figures and checking routine eligibility toward spending choices and difficult customer returns. Decision rights stay within existing delegated limits.

reach.task: Compare category spending scenarios against sales targets.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, forecast uncertainty and the difference between committed spending and cash paid.

reach.task: Resolve routine returns and prepare clear exception requests.
reach.learn: Return eligibility, evidence capture and calm explanations of customer options.

reach.task: Reconcile purchases, returns and outstanding transaction records.
reach.learn: Transaction matching, duplicate detection and stock disposition codes.

evidence.claim: Scheduled financial reports, budget scenarios and transaction checks can use deterministic calculations and rules.
RELEX Solutions supports merchandise forecasting and replenishment; this supports the budget-input capability, not payment or return authorization.
Human decisions can remain in place while software prepares evidence, routes approvals and records authorized actions.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one store or department using existing transaction interfaces, not documented case results.
GDPR applies to customer and employee data. National rules determine any employee consultation obligations for changed workflows.

assumptions: The retailer has 200 to 2,000 staff, with store supervisors operating under centrally defined approval limits.
The {OPS_SYSTEM} slot represents the retail point-of-sale and stock system.
Most routine returns are already handled by sales assistants; supervisor work concentrates on referrals and exceptions.
Payment requests have structured invoice and receipt records in the {ERP} or {PROCUREMENT}.
Finance releases supplier payments separately from the supervisor's spending authorization.
Step shares describe the combined workflow; finance and sales-assistant execution are included as handoffs.
No autonomous agent or model loop is needed for the proposed scope.
The consultation and access estimate includes national-rule screening and consultation where applicable; formal procedures may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which transaction interfaces, approval rules and reporting features are available in the installed systems?
What spending, budget and return decisions may the supervisor authorize?
How often do missing receipts, damaged goods, cash refunds or disputed payments occur?
Can the {OPS_SYSTEM} execute an approved refund without another manual transaction?
How much supervisor time is actually spent on budgets, payments and return exceptions?
Which national rules, employee representation arrangements and consultation procedures apply?
Are payment and refund records sufficiently consistent for reliable matching?
research_questions: Which required controls can be configured before adding custom code?
What transaction identifiers prevent duplicate payments and refunds across retries?
Which return scenarios need physical inspection or a customer conversation?
What evidence and retention periods are required for approval records under applicable rules?
Would any later employee scoring or task-allocation feature change the EU AI Act assessment?
new_work: Resolve failed matches, missing receipt records and stale data feeds.
Maintain budget drivers, approval limits and return-policy rules.
Review refund and payment exceptions, including duplicate prevention failures.
Reconcile approved actions with bank confirmations and stock movements.
Check access permissions, audit records and retention settings after policy or staffing changes.

role.altitude: The supervisor spends more time choosing spending responses and handling difficult returns, with clearer evidence and existing approval rights.
reach: Support sales managers with category spending scenarios.
Help retail salespersons resolve returns consistently.
Work with order clerks on purchase and return reconciliation.
skills_to_grow: Budget scenario analysis and contribution margin.
role.ambitious_version: Run a daily store spending review that identifies emerging overruns early enough to change purchasing priorities within delegated authority.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers
